title: An empty flattened map: both entry points now agree that it is not representable
rationale: The missing/empty-input drill the doctrine requires of every new gate, and a real asymmetry rather than a ceremonial one. It was written to pin a DISAGREEMENT: reconstructToMap early-returned createEmptyRecord for an empty flattened map, which populated only defaulted and nullable fields; reconstruct() then fed that partial map to mapToGenericRecord, whose build() had to answer for a required field with no default. Two sibling methods gave the same input two different answers about whether it is representable - the same shape as avro-flattened-name-collision-guard-fires. That disagreement is repaired in 2.1.0, and this row's continuing job is the other half of its charter: to make sure the empty-map path stays identical to the ordinary path, and to notice immediately if a short-circuit is ever reintroduced.
catchesBugClass: A degenerate-input path that diverges between two public entry points. Now also: the reintroduction of ANY empty-or-null special case in reconstructToMap. Its own previous wording promised to catch 'the empty-map early return being deleted or widened' - the early return was deleted and this row went red on cue, which is the guarantee working rather than a fixture needing repair.
cannotCatch: It cannot tell you whether FAILING is the CORRECT answer for an empty map - it only pins that both entry points now give the same one, and that the message names the field. It does not cover a partially-populated flattened map, which is the far more common Spark case and reaches a different branch. And it says nothing about an all-optional schema, where an empty map still legitimately returns a populated record; that direction is pinned in AvroReconstructorEmptyInputTest so that 'make the empty case loud' cannot be implemented as 'make the empty case always throw'.

predicted.detail: An empty map now takes the ordinary path, so both entry points fail identically with a ReconstructionException naming the required field by its flattened path. Not LOSSLESS: an empty map genuinely cannot produce a record for a schema with a required no-default field, so the loss is in the input rather than in the library.

expected.avroDoc: THROWN: ReconstructionException: Cannot reconstruct com.example.Req: no value in the flattened input and no usable schema default for required field(s) id. Supply the key(s), or allowMissingFields(true) to substitute Avro type defaults.

measurementNote: MOVED DEFECT -> ACCEPTED_LOSS in 2.1.0 by the NP-025 repair, and the PREDICTION WAS REWRITTEN WITH IT rather than left to be papered over by a classificationOverride - an override records measurement correcting a prediction, not a deliberate behaviour change. THE PREDICTION THIS REPLACES, kept verbatim so the repair does not erase it: 'DEFECT - UNCERTAIN AND FLAGGED: depends on what MapFlattener.flatten({}) returns. If it returns an empty map, reconstructToMap early-returns {region:null} and reconstruct() throws on the required id. The recorder decides; if measurement contradicts DEFECT the manifest publishes the measurement and an override records the disagreement.' THE RECORDING THIS REPLACES: avroDoc was 'THROWN: AvroMissingFieldException: Field id type:STRING pos:0 not set and has no default value' - Avro's own exception, leaking from GenericRecordBuilder.build() outside the per-field try, naming the field but never the flattened path. datumChecks were all false then and are all false now.
